lines.en: Mia, the course is almost over. I have learned more than I expected, even though I was tired and busy all spring.
lines.pt: Mia, o curso está quase no fim. Aprendi mais do que esperava, mesmo cansada e ocupada a primavera toda.

lines.en: Me too. I used to mix up make and do, but now I know we make a decision and do the dishes.
lines.pt: Eu também. Eu misturava make e do, mas agora sei que fazemos uma decisão com make e a louça com do.

lines.en: And the words with endings! Yesterday I described our team as hopeful and careful, but a bit careless with deadlines.
lines.pt: E as palavras com terminações! Ontem descrevi nossa equipe como esperançosa e cuidadosa, mas um pouco descuidada com prazos.

lines.en: I have been practicing the verb patterns too. There is no point in arguing, and I can not help laughing at my brother’s jokes.
lines.pt: Tenho praticado os padrões de verbos também. Não adianta discutir, e não consigo evitar rir das piadas do meu irmão.

lines.en: The connectors helped me. Although it rained on Saturday, we had a great time, and I would go even if it snowed.
lines.pt: Os conectores me ajudaram. Embora tenha chovido no sábado, nos divertimos muito, e eu iria mesmo que nevasse.

lines.en: At work I described a chart. I said that sales rose by ten percent and that the number of customers has doubled.
lines.pt: No trabalho descrevi um gráfico. Disse que as vendas subiram dez por cento e que o número de clientes dobrou.

lines.en: Impressive! Was it hard to give your opinion in the meeting? I still find it difficult to say I disagree without sounding rude.
lines.pt: Impressionante! Foi difícil dar sua opinião na reunião? Ainda acho difícil dizer que discordo sem parecer rude.

lines.en: A bit. But “I see your point, but…” and “I am afraid I disagree” help me stay polite and give a reason.
lines.pt: Um pouco. Mas “Entendo seu ponto, mas…” e “Receio discordar” me ajudam a ser educada e dar um motivo.

lines.en: Time is simpler now. I have lived here for ten years, and I will be there by six and wait until seven.
lines.pt: O tempo está mais simples agora. Moro aqui há dez anos e vou estar lá até as seis e esperar até as sete.

lines.en: Then let us celebrate. If we pass the final test, we will have a coffee and plan the next course.
lines.pt: Então vamos comemorar. Se passarmos na prova final, tomaremos um café e planejaremos o próximo curso.

lines.en: Deal. Six weeks ago I could only say simple things, and now I can discuss opinions, numbers and time. I am proud.
lines.pt: Combinado. Seis semanas atrás eu só dizia coisas simples, e agora discuto opiniões, números e tempo. Estou orgulhosa.

compare.ask: I have lived here for ten years.
compare.br: No Brasil, “eu moro aqui há dez anos” usa o presente.
compare.tip: Diga: “I have lived here for ten years.”
compare.us: Em inglês, use o present perfect: I have lived here for ten years. Para o ponto de início, since: I have lived here since 2015.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.

pages.title: I used to mix up make and do · 1/3
paragraphs: Dana and Bia study in Portland. They sit in the classroom. It rains outside. They open old notebooks. Dana asks a question. What have you learned?

“Bia, the course is almost over. I have learned more than I expected, even though I was tired and busy all spring.” says Dana. “Me too. I used to mix up make and do, but now I know we make a decision and do the dishes.” says Bia. “And the words with endings! Yesterday I described our team as hopeful and careful, but a bit careless with deadlines.” says Dana.
